specification.assumptions: Hardware masses, power limits, motor efficiency, material allowables, battery and transition energy are frozen engineering assumptions, not measured aircraft performance.

designs.title: BASELINE
designs.change: Unmodified baseline with fixed 0.5 kg payload and 150 Wh battery. Initial evaluation will establish feasibility, speed, payload capacity and best-cruise drag references.

limitations: No flight validation; transition energy allowance, not dynamic simulation.
VLM/XFOIL attached-flow estimates; no rotor interference, flutter, fatigue or control simulation.
Maximum speed is the highest supported passing speed on a 0.25 m/s grid; no propeller-map extrapolation.
Beam screening excludes joints/local shell buckling; hardware properties are assumptions.

reflection.lesson: Screening estimates show a feasible baseline: 68.03 km at 17 m/s. Reserve and overhead leave ~105 Wh for cruise; hardware/profile drag account for 2.31 of 3.62 N. Static margin is 9.51% (allowed 5–20%). Structure passes: wing stress 118.6 MPa, deflection 37.9 mm. Energy and parasite drag limit range.
reflection.next_focus: Prioritize hardware/profile drag reduction, then cautious mass reduction, retaining the 0.5 kg mission payload and 150 Wh battery. Recheck static margin and structural limits after changes. Protect max speed ≥18.05 m/s and payload capacity ≥0.912 kg (95% of baseline). Repeat adverse-case screening; baseline combined-adverse range is 51.18 km.

Baseline cruise drag was 0.75/0.56/1.11/1.20 N induced/body/profile/hardware; fixed pods and blades remain unchanged. Battery and payload boxes retain 45 mm axial clearance. Recheck wing stiffness before more span/thinning (62.5 mm deflection limit). Protect ≥18.05 m/s and ≥0.912 kg capacity. Validate robustness: combined-adverse estimated range falls to 59.38 km.

designs.change: Target >80.04 km using a broader tapered wing, compact long-nose fuselage, smaller all-moving trim tail and lighter booms. tool.explanation:
This is a constant-cruise energy sensitivity calculator, not a flight simulator. Supply all five inputs; invalid inputs raise ValueError. Reserve is deducted first, then non-cruise overhead. Your history does not explicitly specify reserve_fraction or overhead_wh, so these must be supplied rather than assuming all 150 Wh is available for cruise.

Compare drag improvements by changing cruise_power_w at a matched speed, using an external propulsion-efficiency estimate to translate drag into electrical power. A 10% cruise-power reduction increases range by 11.11% when speed and cruise energy remain unchanged.

Compare hover-energy improvements by changing overhead_wh. For constant hover power, hover energy is hover_power_w * hover_seconds / 3600; include transition and other non-cruise energy as appropriate. Each Wh saved adds 1 / wh_per_km kilometers without changing cruise Wh/km. At iteration 2's cruise point (67.4106 W, 14 m/s), consumption is approximately 1.33751 Wh/km, so saving 1 Wh of overhead adds about 0.748 km.

Your iterations use different cruise speeds, so their changes do not isolate drag reduction alone. This utility does not evaluate geometry, stability, structural limits, or flight feasibility.
